item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Breaks Silence on CHESTER BENNINGTON’s Death: 'Is It Even Called LINKIN PARK Anymore?'
item.description: Linkin Park bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell opened up about the band’s long road back to music after the loss of lead singer Chester Bennington. In a new interview with Czech station Evropa 2 (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: LINKIN PARK Cancels Switzerland Concert After Health Problem in Band: 'We’re Not In A Spot To Perform Tonight'
item.description: Linkin Park called off their performance in Bern, Switzerland just hours before showtime, citing a medical issue within the band. The June 20 concert at Bernexpo was part of the group’s 2025 world tour promoting From Zero, their first album since 2017.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda: “Our New Lineup Came Together Naturally”
item.description: Linkin Park is back. New album (listen below). New lineup. Same vibe. This one’s called “From Zero”, which feels like a bit of an oversell for a band that’s been rehashing itself since 2017.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: Linkin Park's Mike Shinoda: "This Isn’t a Reunion, It’s a New Chapter"
item.description: Mike Shinoda recently shared more details about Linkin Park’s reformation during an interview with BBC Radio 1’s New Music Show With Jack Saunders. The vocalist and multi-instrumentalist pulled back the curtain on how the band’s new chapter began and what fans can expect moving forward.

item.title: Chester Bennington's Mother Accuses Linkin Park of Betrayal
item.description: The rosy glow of Linkin Park’s reunion announcement didn’t last long, did it? The initial buzz around the band’s so-called “new era”—complete with Emily Armstrong as the replacement vocalist—has quickly turned into a storm of controversy and frustration.

item.title: MIKE SHINODA Explains Why LINKIN PARK Kept Their Name: "Changing It Would Be Stupid"
item.description: Linkin Park is back, and the headlines are practically writing themselves. New vocalist? Emily Armstrong. New album? From Zero. New tour? It’s happening. But of course, with all this change, the question isn’t just what they’re doing—it’s why.

item.title: Mike Shinoda Teases “Exciting Things” for Linkin Park Fans
item.description: Reunions? Overdone. Predictable. (Unless it’s the one band you care about—then it’s “historic” and “world-changing,” right?) For years now, Linkin Park has been the one nu-metal heavyweight keeping quiet, while every other act rides the nostalgia wave like it’s 2001.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.
